name: BEFORE & AFTER
scope: Every answer is two known things run together on a word they share — the last word of the first is the first word of the second.

clues.q: Gotham's caped pair, joined to the outlaw of Sherwood Forest
The boy wizard of Hogwarts, joined to the spinning disc a pot is thrown on
The clown who sells hamburgers, joined to the fortieth president
The liner that went down in 1912, joined to a warship's wall of steel
The boundary a black hole allows nothing back across, joined to the formal dance

name: POTPOURRI
scope: Every answer is an ordinary household object. The subjects roam; the answers never leave the house.

clues.q: An everyday thing with a head and teeth and no mouth at all
This cooking vessel takes its name by a long road from the Latin scutella, a little dish
David Smith patented the spring-loaded version of this fastener in 1853
Long before synthetic ones, a dried gourd did this bathroom job
Melville Bissell patented a mechanical one of these in 1876, to get sawdust out of a shop floor

name: WORD ORIGINS
scope: Every answer is where an English word came from — the language it was borrowed out of, or the place or person behind it.

clues.q: Kindergarten arrives in English straight from this language, meaning a garden of children
Sabotage comes from this language's word for a wooden shoe
Assassin traces back to a secretive eleventh-century sect in what is now this country
The name of the citrus fruit reached English from naranj, a word in this language
Shrapnel is named for a gunnery officer who served this country's army

name: WE THE PEOPLE
scope: Every answer is an amendment, a clause, a branch or an office of the US Constitution.

clues.q: The branch of government tasked with making the laws
The amendment guaranteeing freedom of speech, religion, and the press
The article of the Constitution that establishes the executive branch and the presidency
The clause that establishes the Constitution and federal laws as the highest law of the land
The number of state ratifications required for the original Constitution to take effect

name: WORLD HISTORY
scope: Every answer is an empire, a treaty, a revolution or a ruler from world history.

clues.q: The empire Augustus founded out of a republic, which later split in two
The royal document King John of England was forced to seal at Runnymede in 1215
The French monarch overthrown and executed during the 1789 revolution
The devastating European conflict that ended with the Peace of Westphalia in 1648
The final imperial dynasty of China, which fell to a republic in 1912

name: LITERATURE
scope: Every answer is a work of literature, its author, or a character or place from one.

clues.q: The English playwright and poet who wrote Romeo and Juliet and Hamlet
The whaling captain obsessed with hunting down the white whale in Moby-Dick
The dystopian novel by George Orwell featuring the watchful eyes of Big Brother
The author of the 19th-century Russian psychological masterpiece Crime and Punishment
The fictional town at the heart of Gabriel Garcia Marquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude

name: SPORTS
scope: Every answer is a sport, a rule of one, a trophy or a position.

clues.q: The sport where professional teams compete annually for the Super Bowl
The international tennis tournament played on red clay courts in Paris
The most clubs a golfer may carry in the bag during a round
The large silver trophy awarded annually to the National Hockey League champion
The Olympic event that runs fencing, swimming, equestrian, shooting and running together

name: U.S. PRESIDENTS
scope: Every answer is a US president or something one of them did.

clues.q: The first president of the United States and commander of the Continental Army
The president who delivered the Gettysburg Address during the American Civil War
The only US president to resign the office
The president who signed the Federal Reserve Act into law in 1913
The first president to serve two terms that did not run back to back
